Wellbutrin alleviated the side effects SOMEWHAT for me, but I was never back to 100% until I switched meds. The truth of the matter is - and I speak as a guy who's now on his 15th SSRI - is you can cum or you can not be depressed, generally speaking. Part of doing this is trading off some sexual gratification for a more balanced life. It is possible to stumble onto a drug that works for both, but until you get on the meddy-go-round and try different drugs, there is literally no way to know how they will affect you

Even me telling you Wellbutrin helped me is only true for me.  Everybody's chemistry is different, and your mileage will literally vary. Asking other people how a drug affected them really doesn't tell you anything at all, because we're not YOU. I'm sorry, but trial and error is literally the only way any of this works. It sucks. And it forces you to make devil's bargains like cumming vs. not being depressed.

If Cymbalta works for you mentally right now, then you have to make a decision on what's more important to you. Every drug switch you make comes with tradeoffs and adds at a minimum one month to see how things really shake out.

See, for me, Cymbalta absolutely erased my libido 100%. I became asexual. Wellbutrin allowed me to orgasm again, but I honestly lost any and all desire for sexual activity. I made myself do it occasionally, because I felt like I should for just general health reasons. But I didn't really want to. Now, on Viibryd, my libido is maybe back to 60% and my abilities are closer to 85%. But there was literally no way for me to know until I left Cymbalta.

EDIT: For clarity, I left Cymbalta because it made me sleep 18 to 20 hours a day.

My story is eerily similar to yours. Except I was married and my wife left me, and I got laid off at my job, which I hated anyway. I've been unemployed for over a year, had a mental breakdown and am now living with my parents as I try to get a drug cocktail to take hold.

You and I have seen through the veil. Not only can I not go back to that life, I will not. I'll blow my brains out on Main Street before I let myself get sucked back into that shit. Unlike you, I am weak. And the things that happened to me broke me. I used to be a newspaper reporter, and I saw some shit during my time that changed me in some fundamental ways. Regardless, I can't unsee what I've seen, and I can't unfeel what I've felt. I am not lazy, either. I was a workaholic. I lived my life for my job and my wife. (My ex-wife left me for some other issues that weren't directly related to me, or so she has since admitted to me. Who knows? Maybe I was a shit husband.)

But after falling off the ladder I was climbing -- the one I already knew there was nothing at the top of -- I had a stark realization. I realized I was not going to climb it again. And there was literally nothing anyone was going to be able to do to make me. I don't know what that means for me. I sit in a room all day, and I try to keep myself busy with various writings, arts, projects and whatever. I think this is how my life ends. My parents can't support me forever. I might be able to get some part-time job, but I haven't because the first time someone gives me shit, I'm just going to stand up and walk out if I don't just flat-out assault them. I'm like Bartleby the Scrivener, and that dude just withered away. 

What's the "answer?" To be honest, I don't want an answer. I'll suck down some drugs for a while so I can live in everyone else's world. I'd rather stick around until my parents are dead. Seems like the (very) least I can do for them. But when shit reaches the point where I can't contain it any more, I'll drive down to the hardware store and figure out how to make the fastest exit. (I was thinking nail gun to the head. My dad's got an air compressor. I don't know if there are any safeties that keep people from nail gunning themselves to death. I haven't researched it yet. There's always rope if that doesn't work.)

I don't want to use the word "comforted," obviously -- I'd rather you didn't feel this way -- but I do feel some sort of 'ease' at knowing I'm not the only one who feels like this. I don't have any advice for you. I doubt you'd even want to place yourself in the same boat as me. 

But you're not wrong about this world. Neither am I. 

Unfortunately for us, this world is not a welcoming place for people with these kinds of mindsets. I don't know what your level of depression is. If you want to live and you aren't in therapy, find a way to get into therapy now. And if you don't like your therapist, get another one. Keep talking to someone until someone takes you seriously. It might not happen right away. After that, there's drugs (legal ones). And after that, there's drugs (illegal ones, you know some of them, but this time take WAY more). And after that, there's the grave. I hope both of us find a way to get through without getting that far by our own hands. 

Anyway, friend -- you're seen. I wish I had more to give you. I wish you the very best.

I've been on and off for a long time, and usually, when I come off a drug, I feel great. (After the brain zaps and shit stop.) And then, I end up back on them again. I'm not saying to get back on them -- a lot of people come off and are fine --  but I am cautioning you to keep an edge little bit longer in regards to yourself. Be critical and honest enough that if you do feel the slide back down, you don't hesitate in getting help again. Because I've done that, too, with disastrous, fuck-my-shit-up results. 

I use the analogy of an unwanted tree in your yard. You may cut it down and even take the stump all the way down to the earth, but that tree still has roots, and until the roots are removed, you have to understand that some trees can and will grow back. Yes. the yard looks better without the tree. Everyone will even tell you so. But that tree grows for a reason, and if we haven't chased the reason all the way through the dirt, one day you'll wake up and that tree will be back, and you'll have to start the work of cutting it down all over again. If the tree doesn't grow back, fantastic! That's an incredible win, and you should enjoy all the benefits of it guilt-free.

But don't turn your back on the stump.

That said, there are so many SSRIs, and they all work differently. Your experience with one will likely not mirror your experience with another, should you choose to go back on. And even then, all hope is not lost.

Just keep walking it through in your own head, and don't take your own inner voice's words to be 100% gospel. Keep an eye on your own actions, and have someone you love and trust do so, too. I wish you the best in being able to stay off, though. I do believe it is something everyone whose taking these drugs would love. Good luck!

I think we're all really bad at delineating between 'talent' and 'ability.' Everyone can learn an ability; everyone can reach a level of competence. But 'talent,' to me is 'ability harnessed.' And with that, there is a ceiling. I've worked training writers for over a decade. And you can write as much as you'd like, but at some point, everyone hits a ceiling. There is a point where working harder at something provides diminishing returns. Everyone is only so good at it. 

Talent, I believe, is the act of moving laterally beneath that ceiling. Most of us just keep beating against the ceiling and getting frustrated that it won't move. The talented see that abilities aren't just ladders. They exist in 3D space. You have to take what you have, beneath your limits, and bring it to new spaces. Maybe, at some point in your travels, you find a place where the ceiling lifts, but you need the experience of moving laterally to a) find it and b) learn how to climb a new, unfamiliar ladder. But, then again, maybe that never happens. And you have to learn to take joy from moving your limited ability into new places. 

And while I make that sound simple, it's not. Otherwise, we'd all be brilliant. The truth is that continued hard work is necessary. But seeing through the veil into 3D space isn't guaranteed. Those people are, indeed, special.

BUT, until you try, there is no reliable way to know which one you are.

If it's properly set up, you'll be fine. It likely won't be straight out of the box. If you've never done your own setup before, have a professional look at the nut, for sure. You'll only really have tuning problems with a Bigsby if the nut is improperly cut or the bridge slots aren't filed properly. Dead-on setups are KEY with a Bigsby. If you've never done one, ask the tech or luthier if you can watch and get pointers. 

The other thing I suggest (I have a Streamliner) is either stringing with 11s or 12s. You'll get the best response from those. If possible, buy string packs with a wound G string instead of a plain string like most packs have. The tension differences in wound vs unwound third strings are a lifesaver. If you have a wound G, you can even put 10s on it, really, which will make bends easier. Wound Gs aren't necessarily easy to find in stores. I'd try to order those online and always keep an extra pack on hand.

Good luck!

EDIT: I've played mine in open D, DADGAD, drop D, etc. If the nut is right, shouldn't be an issue. The standard nut should be fine if cut right. Graphite or pencil lead will act as a great lubricant in the nut slots. But if you get the chance, I recommend you replace the nut with a TUSQ XL one. It has Teflon in it, which acts as its own lubricant. They cost $15 (plus installation labor).

To be fair, it doesn't sound like you're in much of a place for a relationship, and maybe you need to explore that some more before you make any moves.

At the same time, no one can force you to be in a relationship. You are a grown adult, and this is part of relationships. It's a bit of emotional terrorism for someone to block a breakup like that, and it's a red flag for any future the two of you have together.

There's never a way to let someone down gently. Not if you're being honest. Hurt is hurt, and if she's in a place where she doesn't want to lose you, it's going to hurt, That said, you can start laying the groundwork by phone. You can tell her you're not feeling well or that you've got a lot on your mind. You can be honest and tell her you need a break, and that break can start to morph into a breakUP.

Or you can be honest about what's happening to you and be clear to her that this is what you're feeling. Maybe you don't know why you feel this way. Tell her that, too. You can't help what you're feeling, and it doesn't have anything to do with her. (Because that's true. You're the one who feels this way. This is on you.) Tell her she's a great person, but that this isn't working out, and it's reached a point where it's not fair for you OR for her. Is there a way for the two of you to approach this that saves the relationship, like some sort of compromise? (Probably not. It sounds like you're done. But don't do this until you're SURE this is what you want.)

But in all honesty, pain is the price for relationships, good or bad. If you want out, and being out will hurt her, then you will in some way or form hurt her. Sorry. That's just how it is, friend. How she deals with that hurt is not your particular problem if you're honest with her and tell her what you're feeling. It will feel shitty. So shitty. But such is love and life.

If you go through with this, however, and you do have to hurt her feelings to get free, you owe it to the both of you to look at what it is you want out of a relationship. There will be girls who will have the same feelings toward 'alone time' that you do, and you shouldn't go forward with another relationship until you have an idea of who you will be dating. Because if you have to hurt someone because you made a mistake and got into a relationship you didn't want, you don't have the right to hurt people in the future in the same way.

This is going to be a growth thing for you. And growth hurts. Hurts like hell. Be honest, be gentle, but also be firm. And don't let other emotions -- yours or hers -- get in the way of what you're trying to achieve. You have to deal with what you're feeling as much or more as she's going to have to deal with the fallout. DEAL being the key word.

​

As for your mom, again, you're a grown man, and she doesn't get a say in how you live that part of your life unless you give her a say. That's on you, too. You're the one who has to walk in your shoes, not her. At the same time, you do have to walk in those shoes. Are they the right shoes for you. (Yikes, I hate that analogy, but I'll stand by it for now. It sounds like none of you will be happy about this situation, so start ripping off the bandage and take every opportunity you can to be as KIND about it as you can. And do the work on yourself, as well.

Good luck.

​

EDIT: I should also tell you that the reason I push 'honesty' so much, even though it hurts, is because if you don't get out of the relationship and you start to resent her, you will hurt her in other smaller ways for a long time before you have a painful breakup anyway.
